topic: Change of Basis: A Tale of Two Grids

sections.title: The Hook: Same Point, Different Perspectives
lecture_lines: Alice uses a standard square coordinate grid.
She sees a point at coordinates three-two.
Bob uses a tilted and stretched coordinate grid.
He sees the same point at coordinate one-one.
Coordinates depend on the perspective you choose.
animations: Fade in a standard white Cartesian grid (#FFFFFF).
Create a red dot (#FF0000) at coordinates (3, 2).
Add a white text label "(3, 2)" next to the dot.
Overlay a tilted yellow grid (#FFFF00) representing Bob's perspective.
Change the dot's label to yellow "(1, 1)" while keeping the dot in place.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
lecture_lines: A basis is a set of spanning vectors.
Standard unit vectors are i-hat and j-hat.
Every vector is a recipe of basis vectors.
animations: Draw green vector i (#00FF00) and blue vector j (#0000FF).
Draw a white vector (#FFFFFF) extending from origin to (3, 2).

Scale and move 3 i-vectors and 2 j-vectors to form the white vector, incorporating the recipe icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/recipe.svg] to represent the combination of components.

sections.title: Introducing the Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: We describe Bob's basis vectors using Alice's grid.
These descriptions become the columns of transition matrix P.
This matrix P translates between Bob and Alice.
animations: Draw [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bob.svg]'s basis vectors b1 [2, 1] (#FFFF00) and b2 [-1, 1] (#FF00FF).
Create a matrix P with columns [2, 1] and [-1, 1].
Flash the colors of b1/b2 and their corresponding matrix columns.

sections.title: The Transformation Formula
lecture_lines: Bob's coordinates are transformed using this matrix formula.
We start with Bob's coordinate point at one-one.
Multiplying by P warps Bob's grid into Alice's.
The calculation results in Alice's coordinates one-two.
The point now matches Alice's standard grid perspective.
animations: Show Bob's [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bob.svg] yellow grid (#FFFF00) with a point at (1, 1).
Write the formula "v_std = P * v_alt" in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the "v_alt" part of the formula in yellow (#FFFF00).
Transform the yellow grid into a white standard grid (#FFFFFF).
Move the point to (1, 2) on the white grid.

sections.title: The Inverse: Returning to the Alternate Basis
lecture_lines: Let's go backwards using Alice's point at one-two.
We use the inverse of the transition matrix P.
Multiplying by P-inverse transforms Alice's coordinates back.
Alice's standard grid squishes to match Bob's perspective.
The point arrives at its coordinate one-one for Bob.
animations: Show the standard white grid (#FFFFFF) with a point at (1, 2).
Write the formula "v_alt = P_inv * v_std" in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the "v_std" part of the formula in white (#FFFFFF).
Transform the white grid into the yellow tilted grid (#FFFF00).
Move the point to (1, 1) on the yellow grid.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Intuition
lecture_lines: Change of basis simplifies many complex mathematical problems.
It's like switching languages to describe the same world.
Choosing the right basis reveals hidden structures.
animations: Show a 4x4 grid of gray squares (#888888) representing pixels.
Morph the squares into 4 different colored wave patterns (#00FFFF, #FF00FF, #FFFF00, #00FF00).
Fade in text "Simpler Representation" in white (#FFFFFF).
